executive_assessment.text: Province-specific nearby cyclone metrics differ from the Tongariki/Buninga water-access case and project design; water-system completion is unverified.
Displacement safeguards address land/consent risks, while the ministry reports distinct transport and political barriers to climate-project implementation.
The pooled study found no significant aggregate association, with important geographic and methodological limits.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-09-18 reports: During 1971–2021, the study counted 2.31 cyclone tracks per season within 500 km of Torba, 2.30 of Sanma and 2.45 of Penama.
Source dated 2025-09-18 reports: The severe-cyclone share rose in all six provinces; mean wind-speed increases were significant for Tafea (18.1%), Penama (13.4%) and Shefa (13.0%).

Source dated 2025-09-18 reports: Under CMIP5 RCP8.5, the illustrative severe-cyclone intensity of Pam has a shorter projected return period in 2071–2100 than 1971–2000: 77 to 62 years in Torba and 68 to 51 in Penama.

Source dated 2025-03-25 reports: The UNDP account attributes clean-water difficulty on Tongariki and Buninga to saltwater intrusion from rising seas; the boat-accessible islands lack natural streams and rely on rainwater.

Source dated 2025-03-25 reports: Residents walk long distances in intense heat carrying water containers that can exceed 20 kg; the account says this is especially treacherous for older people and people with disabilities.

Source dated 2025-03-25 reports: A locally assessed rainwater system was designed for 134 households (107 Tongariki; 27 Buninga), with raised and reinforced tanks; materials had arrived, but household service was still a future hope.
Source dated 2024 reports: In 2024, 23 of 29 Area Council climate officers were in place; 40 communities developed adaptation plans, while final documentation remained due in 2025.
Source dated 2024 reports: Two solar freezers were procured for fisheries cold storage in Mota Lava and Mataso/Makira.
Source dated 2024 reports: A solar dryer pilot for root crops and vegetables was introduced in Nguna/Pele.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 20 of 20 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No countrywide causal estimate of climate impacts on conflict or violence is established by these sources.
Full subnational coverage and independently evaluated long-term response effectiveness remain gaps.
Earthquakes and volcanic events in the multi-hazard results story are not treated as climate impacts.
No verified local climate-conflict pathway was established in the inspected material.

National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
The ADB multi-hazard assessment for Luganville and a disability-inclusion report were inaccessible (403); indexed material was not used as evidence.
SPREP's linked Van-KIRAP extreme-flood analysis download yielded only its cover, so Port Vila/Luganville flood findings could not be directly checked.
The accessible CSIRO/VMGD Vanuatu North regional climate summary was excluded from findings because its rights notice requires written permission to reproduce or copy material.

No directly read local source established a climate-triggered violent-conflict event. The 2018 policy and pooled research provide conditional and non-detection evidence with the stated limits, not proof of absence.
Political instability and airline liquidation are separate implementation barriers; neither should be relabelled armed conflict.
No additional pathway is forced from the pooled non-detection study or generic co-occurrence.
